investigations.name: 01-erdos-renyi-random-growth
investigations.description:
Random growth produces a homogeneous, hub-free network (Poisson-like degrees) — the null baseline the structured rules are read against.

The network is stored as process-bigraph node/edge maps and reconfigured each step by the `erdos_renyi` reaction (emitting _add/_remove structural sentinels). The animation and GIF in viz/ show the evolution; scalar metrics are emitted for the behavior tests.
investigations.title: Erdős–Rényi random growth
investigations.objective: What topology emerges when edges form purely at random, with no preference?
investigations.claim: Random growth produces a homogeneous, hub-free network (Poisson-like degrees) — the null baseline the structured rules are read against.

investigations.name: 02-preferential-attachment
investigations.description:
Degree-proportional attachment produces scale-free hubs with a power-law degree tail — unlike random growth.

The network is stored as process-bigraph node/edge maps and reconfigured each step by the `preferential_attachment` reaction (emitting _add/_remove structural sentinels). The animation and GIF in viz/ show the evolution; scalar metrics are emitted for the behavior tests.
investigations.title: Barabási–Albert preferential attachment
investigations.objective: Does degree-proportional attachment produce scale-free hubs?
investigations.claim: Degree-proportional attachment produces scale-free hubs with a power-law degree tail — unlike random growth.

investigations.name: 03-small-world-rewiring
investigations.description:
Random rewiring of a ring lattice preserves edge count while shortcuts collapse path length — producing the small-world regime.

The network is stored as process-bigraph node/edge maps and reconfigured each step by the `small_world_rewire` reaction (emitting _add/_remove structural sentinels). The animation and GIF in viz/ show the evolution; scalar metrics are emitted for the behavior tests.
investigations.title: Watts–Strogatz small-world rewiring
investigations.objective: How does random rewiring of a ring lattice change its structure?
investigations.claim: Random rewiring of a ring lattice preserves edge count while shortcuts collapse path length — producing the small-world regime.

investigations.name: 04-fitness-condensation
investigations.description:
Fitness-weighted attachment still builds hubs, but a high-fitness latecomer can overtake older nodes — unlike pure Barabási–Albert.

The network is stored as process-bigraph node/edge maps and reconfigured each step by the `fitness_attachment` reaction (emitting _add/_remove structural sentinels). The animation and GIF in viz/ show the evolution; scalar metrics are emitted for the behavior tests.
investigations.title: Bianconi–Barabási fitness attachment
investigations.objective: Can an intrinsic node fitness let a latecomer overtake older, higher-degree nodes?
investigations.claim: Fitness-weighted attachment still builds hubs, but a high-fitness latecomer can overtake older nodes — unlike pure Barabási–Albert.

investigations.name: 05-duplication-divergence
investigations.description:
Copy-then-diverge growth reproduces the heavy-tailed, locally clustered topology seen in protein-interaction networks.

The network is stored as process-bigraph node/edge maps and reconfigured each step by the `duplication_divergence` reaction (emitting _add/_remove structural sentinels). The animation and GIF in viz/ show the evolution; scalar metrics are emitted for the behavior tests.
investigations.title: Duplication–divergence (biological growth)
investigations.objective: Does genome-style duplication-and-divergence reproduce protein-network topology?
investigations.claim: Copy-then-diverge growth reproduces the heavy-tailed, locally clustered topology seen in protein-interaction networks.

investigations.name: 06-forest-fire-densification
investigations.description:
Forest-fire growth densifies the network: mean degree rises as the graph grows, reproducing the densification law.

The network is stored as process-bigraph node/edge maps and reconfigured each step by the `forest_fire` reaction (emitting _add/_remove structural sentinels). The animation and GIF in viz/ show the evolution; scalar metrics are emitted for the behavior tests.
investigations.title: Forest-fire growth & densification
investigations.objective: Does recursive forest-fire burning densify the network over time?
investigations.claim: Forest-fire growth densifies the network: mean degree rises as the graph grows, reproducing the densification law.

investigations.name: 07-adaptive-coevolution
investigations.description:
Coevolving opinions and rewiring self-organise the network into like-minded clusters — topology and state adapt to each other.

The network is stored as process-bigraph node/edge maps and reconfigured each step by the `adaptive_rewire` reaction (emitting _add/_remove structural sentinels). The animation and GIF in viz/ show the evolution; scalar metrics are emitted for the behavior tests.
investigations.title: Adaptive coevolution (opinions + rewiring)
investigations.objective: When topology and node state co-adapt, does the network organise into like-minded communities?
investigations.claim: Coevolving opinions and rewiring self-organise the network into like-minded clusters — topology and state adapt to each other.

investigations.name: 08-activity-driven-temporal
investigations.description:
Activity-driven firing produces a sparse, blinking temporal network — each snapshot is instantaneous, unlike the accreting Family-A graphs.

The network is stored as process-bigraph node/edge maps and reconfigured each step by the `activity_driven` reaction (emitting _add/_remove structural sentinels). The animation and GIF in viz/ show the evolution; scalar metrics are emitted for the behavior tests.
investigations.title: Activity-driven temporal network
investigations.objective: What does an activity-driven contact sequence look like, where edges last only one time window?
investigations.claim: Activity-driven firing produces a sparse, blinking temporal network — each snapshot is instantaneous, unlike the accreting Family-A graphs.

investigations.name: 09-sbml-nodes-coupled
investigations.description:
With an SBML Repressilator at each node and protein diffusion along the edges, the coupled oscillators synchronise — across-node concentration spread collapses.

Each node runs the Repressilator SBML model integrated by COPASI (reusing viva-copasi); the NetworkTransport process diffuses proteins along edges. Reaction and diffusion are combined by operator splitting each tick. See viz/ for the concentration-on-network animation and the per-node time series.
investigations.title: SBML reactors on a network — diffusive coupling synchronises
investigations.objective: When a continuous SBML oscillator runs at every node and species diffuse along the edges, does the network synchronise?
investigations.claim: With an SBML Repressilator at each node and protein diffusion along the edges, the coupled oscillators synchronise — across-node concentration spread collapses.

investigations.name: 10-sbml-nodes-uncoupled
investigations.description:
With diffusion off, the per-node oscillators remain independent and out of phase — the control that isolates coupling as the cause of synchronisation in study 09.

Each node runs the Repressilator SBML model integrated by COPASI (reusing viva-copasi); the NetworkTransport process diffuses proteins along edges. Reaction and diffusion are combined by operator splitting each tick. See viz/ for the concentration-on-network animation and the per-node time series.
investigations.title: SBML reactors on a network — uncoupled control (no diffusion)
investigations.objective: With diffusion switched off, do the per-node oscillators stay out of phase?
investigations.claim: With diffusion off, the per-node oscillators remain independent and out of phase — the control that isolates coupling as the cause of synchronisation in study 09.

investigations.name: 11-coevolving-growing-network
investigations.description:
Continuous SBML dynamics run correctly on a network being built node-by-node by a PBG reaction; each newcomer entrains, and the growing network synchronises.

This is a Family-C (co-evolution) study: a Family-A reaction reconfigures the graph WHILE the Family-B SBML reactors + inter-node transport run on it. See viz/ for the concentration-on-network animation and the per-node time series.
investigations.title: Dynamics on a growing network — reactors entrain as the graph is built
investigations.objective: Can SBML reactor dynamics run on a network whose topology is itself being built by a process-bigraph reaction, and do newcomers entrain?
investigations.claim: Continuous SBML dynamics run correctly on a network being built node-by-node by a PBG reaction: the system stays bounded and oscillating, and most newcomers entrain through the dense local coupling — but synchronisability is topology-dependent, with weakly-attached (low-degree) nodes lagging the synchronised core.

investigations.name: 12-coevolving-rewiring-network
investigations.description:
Coupled SBML oscillators synchronise and stay synchronised even as the coupling edges are continuously rewired — reaction–diffusion is robust to an evolving (but well-connected) topology.

This is a Family-C (co-evolution) study: a Family-A reaction reconfigures the graph WHILE the Family-B SBML reactors + inter-node transport run on it. See viz/ for the concentration-on-network animation and the per-node time series.
investigations.title: Dynamics on a rewiring network — synchrony survives continual rewiring
investigations.objective: Do the coupled oscillators stay synchronised when the very edges that couple them are continuously rewired?
investigations.claim: Coupled SBML oscillators synchronise and stay synchronised even as the coupling edges are continuously rewired — reaction–diffusion is robust to an evolving (but well-connected) topology.

investigations.name: 13-quorum-sensing-coupling
investigations.description:
Proposed follow-up seeded from study 09. Replaces all-protein diffusion with biologically-realistic quorum-sensing coupling via one autoinducer.

(Baseline points at the composite this proposal would EXTEND; the new mechanism is not yet built.)
investigations.title: Quorum-sensing coupling (proposed)
investigations.objective: Does coupling through a single diffusible signal molecule synchronise the networked reactors as effectively as diffusing the internal proteins?

investigations.name: 14-brusselator-model-agnostic
investigations.description:
Proposed follow-up seeded from study 11. Demonstrates the node model is a plug-in, not hardcoded.

(Baseline points at the composite this proposal would EXTEND; the new mechanism is not yet built.)
investigations.title: Model-agnostic node reactor — Brusselator (proposed)
investigations.objective: Is the SBML-at-nodes architecture model-agnostic — does swapping the Repressilator for a Brusselator reproduce reaction–diffusion patterning on the network with no code change?

investigations.name: 15-sbml-adaptive-coevolution
investigations.description:
Proposed follow-up seeded from study 07. The continuous-state analogue of adaptive coevolution: the richest point in the OF↔ON feedback loop.

(Baseline points at the composite this proposal would EXTEND; the new mechanism is not yet built.)
investigations.title: SBML-driven adaptive coevolution (proposed)
investigations.objective: When the continuous node state (an SBML readout) itself drives the rewiring, does a self-organised modular topology emerge?
